title: Chat messaging
summary: Persistent connections, ordering, delivery receipts and offline sync.
prompt: Design a chat app with one-to-one and small group conversations (up to 500 members), online presence, delivery and read receipts, and history that syncs across a user’s devices.

requirements: Functional: send and receive messages in real time, sync history on every device, receipts, presence, push notifications when offline.
Non-functional: low delivery latency (~100s of ms), no lost acknowledged messages, per-conversation ordering, highly available.
Clarify: end-to-end encryption, media (assume uploaded separately and sent as links), retention.
estimation: 200M daily users × 20 messages ≈ 4B messages a day ≈ 46,000/s average; peaks 2–3×.
~200 bytes per message ≈ 800 GB a day of new history before replication.
30M concurrent connections ÷ ~100k per gateway ≈ 300 gateway servers, plus headroom.
api: A WebSocket per device: send {clientMsgId, conversationId, body}; server replies ack {messageId, seq}.
Server pushes message, receipt and presence events; clients ack up to a sequence number.
data: messages partitioned by conversation_id, clustered by seq: (conversation_id, seq, message_id, sender, body, sent_at).
Per-conversation sequence numbers give a total order inside each conversation; there is no global order.
inbox_state(user_id, conversation_id, last_delivered_seq, last_read_seq) drives unread counts and receipts.
Connection registry: user_id/device → gateway, in an in-memory store with TTL heartbeats.
design: Devices connect to gateways through a layer-4 load balancer. Gateways hold connections only; chat services hold logic.
Send: the gateway forwards to the chat service, which deduplicates by clientMsgId, assigns the next seq, persists, acks the sender, then publishes for fan-out.
Fan-out: look up each member’s connected devices in the registry and route to their gateways; offline devices get a push notification and sync later.
deepDives: Ordering: one writer per conversation (route by conversation ID) assigns seq; alternatively use the database’s conditional insert on (conversation, seq).
Exactly-once display from at-least-once delivery: clients deduplicate by message_id and fill gaps by fetching after their last seq.
Reconnect storms after a gateway dies: clients reconnect with jittered backoff and catch up from their last acknowledged seq.
Groups: write the message once and fan out on read, or write per-member inbox pointers; at 500 members, fan-out of notifications (not copies of the message) is fine.
bottlenecks: Presence is chatty: send it only to contacts with an open chat view, batch updates, and tolerate staleness.
Hot group conversations: one sequencer per conversation limits throughput; that is fine at 500 members.
Cross-region users: home each conversation in one region and replicate.
tradeoffs: Per-conversation ordering instead of a global order keeps sequencing scalable.
Storing one copy per conversation saves space; per-user inbox copies make reads faster but multiply writes.
End-to-end encryption protects users but moves search and multi-device key management to clients.

rubric.text: Used persistent connections with a gateway layer and a connection registry.
Defined per-conversation ordering with sequence numbers.
Acknowledged only after persisting; deduplicated by client message ID.
Designed offline delivery: push plus catch-up sync by sequence.
Modelled receipts and unread state per user and conversation.
Sized connections, message rate and storage.
Handled gateway failure and reconnect storms.
Discussed multi-region homing and encryption trade-offs.
